'''Martin Maechler''' (spelled Mächler in the original German) is a Swiss computational statistician and a professor emeritus at [[ETH Zurich]] (Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Zurich). He has worked as a co-developer of [[R (programming language)|R]], a widely used environment for statistical computing and graphics, and is a long-time member of the R Core Development Team.<ref name="R_pioneer">{{Cite web |date=2014-01-13 |title=The R pioneer |url=https://ethz.ch/staffnet/en/news-and-events/internal-news/archive/2014/01/the-r-pioneer.html |access-date=2025-12-14 |website=Staffnet |language=en}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Maechler pursued his academic studies at ETH Zurich, earning a Ph.D. in mathematics in 1989 focusing on [[nonparametric regression]] and [[curve fitting|curve estimation]]. His doctoral advisors were [[Frank Hampel]] and [[Hans-Rudolf Künsch]].<ref name="MGP">{{Cite web |title=Martin Mächler - The Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=84452 |access-date=2025-12-14 |website=www.mathgenealogy.org}}</ref> He conducted post-doctoral research at the [[University of Washington]]'s Department of Statistics for a year from August 1989 and another year at Bell Communications Research, Morristown, NJ.<ref name="ResearchGate">{{Cite web |title=Martin MÄCHLER {{!}} Professor {{!}} Ph.D. math {{!}} ETH Zurich, Zürich {{!}} ETH Zürich {{!}} Department of Mathematics {{!}} Research profile |url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Martin-Maechler |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241227002802/https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Martin-Maechler |archive-date=2024-12-27 |access-date=2025-12-14 |website=ResearchGate |language=en}}</ref>

He has dedicated most of his professional career to ETH Zurich's Seminar for Statistics, serving as a Senior Scientist and Lecturer before becoming an adjunct professor, and has been emeritus since March 2024. <ref name="R_pioneer"/><ref name="ETH_homepage">{{Cite web |title=ETH :: D-MATH -- SfS :: Prof. em. Dr. Martin Mächler |url=https://people.math.ethz.ch/~maechler/ |access-date=2025-12-14 |website=people.math.ethz.ch}}</ref> His primary areas of research and teaching include computational statistics, robust statistical methods, clustering algorithms, and numerical computations, particularly with matrices.<ref name="ResearchGate"/><ref name="ETH_homepage"/>

==R Project involvement==
Maechler is considered a pioneer in the development of the R programming language.<ref name="R_pioneer"/> He joined the R Project in 1995 shortly after its inception, drawn by the open-source nature of the environment and its origin in the ACM award winning [[S_programming language]]. His motivation was to "create something meaningful for mankind," particularly aiding universities in poorer countries that benefit from the open-source model.<ref name="R_pioneer"/>

He is a member of the R Core Development Team and serves as the Secretary General of the [[R Foundation]].<ref name="ResearchGate"/><ref name="ETH_homepage"/> Maechler has authored/maintained numerous R packages, including:<ref name="RDocumentation">{{Cite web |title=Martin Maechler {{!}} Collaborator - RDocumentation |url=https://www.rdocumentation.org/collaborators/name/Martin%20Maechler |access-date=2025-12-14 |website=www.rdocumentation.org}}</ref>
* <code>Matrix</code>: for [[sparse matrix|sparse]] and dense matrix classes.
* <code>cluster</code>: provides methods for cluster analysis.
* <code>robustbase</code>: offering fundamental robust statistical methods.

Maechler is also a key figure in the development of [[Emacs Speaks Statistics]] (ESS), an add-on for the [[GNU Emacs]] text editor that provides dedicated support for statistical programming languages like R. He has been an ESS Core Developer since around 1997 and served as the project leader since 2004.<ref name="ETH_homepage"/>

==Selected publications==
Maechler has co-authored publications and R packages in the domain of linear and generalized linear [[mixed-effects models]]. One of his highly cited works is the R package <code>lme4</code>.<ref name="GoogleScholar">{{cite web |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=krIBxQgAAAAJ&hl=en |title=Martin Mächler - Google Scholar |publisher=Google Scholar |accessdate=2025-12-14}}</ref> He has also contributed to the field of [[data visualization]] with the <code>scatterplot3d</code> package.<ref name="GoogleScholar"/>

==Personal life==
Martin Maechler is married and has two grown sons. He is an active member of his local church and served as a member of Zurich's city council for the [[Evangelical People's Party of Switzerland]] (EVP/PEV) from 2008 to 2014. His hobbies include cross-country skiing, jogging, swimming, hiking, reading, and listening to music.<ref name="ETH_homepage"/><ref name="ETH_history">{{Cite web |title=Who `is' Martin Mächler ? |url=https://people.math.ethz.ch/~maechler/index-2004.html |access-date=2025-12-14 |website=people.math.ethz.ch}}</ref>
